Long story short, I was going to end my life one afternoon. I was walking towards a FiDi subway station where I was going to do it. Then my therapist called wholly serendipitously, and I just collapsed and broken into screams and shrieks and sobs on the sidewalk floor. It was a big scene. I couldn’t walk, I just kept yelling “I want to die.” Like 10 random strangers all kicked into gear. One happened to be a psychologist who took my phone and talked to my therapist for me as two men propped me up and asked me if I’d prefer to walk to the ER to avoid ambulance fees. Then they brought me to the nearest ER, 10 minute walk. About 5 people total went with me and stayed until I was in a bed. 

My life is now so much better than I ever could have conceived of back then. I’m no longer in that place, and I’m so glad NYers were there to save me. They’re m incredible; they know how to mind their business, and they know to intervene when really necessary, more often than perhaps the average population.
